worksheet.title: Worksheet — शल्यचिकित्साजनकः सुश्रुतः (NIOS Sanskrit 309, Chapter 21)
worksheet.instructions: Attempt all questions. Write Sanskrit words in Devanagari and explanations in English. All procedures are to be discussed as HISTORY of Indian science, not as medical guidance. Refer to the lesson text where needed.

questions.question: सुश्रुतः कः आसीत्? कुत्र न्यवसत्? कस्य शिष्यः आसीत्? (Who was Sushruta? Where did he live? Whose disciple was he?) Answer in 2-3 simple Sanskrit sentences or in English.
questions.answer: सुश्रुतः प्राचीनभारतस्य महान् शल्यवैद्यः आसीत्। सः वाराणसीनगरे गङ्गायाः तीरे न्यवसत्। सः काशिराजस्य दिवोदासस्य धन्वन्तरेः शिष्यः आसीत्। (Sushruta was a great surgeon of ancient India; he lived in Varanasi on the bank of the Ganga and was the disciple of Divodasa Dhanvantari, king of Kashi.)
questions.explanation: Basic recall of the three life facts from paragraph 1 of the lesson.

questions.question: यन्त्र और शस्त्र में अन्तर लिखत — What is the difference between यन्त्र and शस्त्र in the Sushruta-Samhita? Give their numbers and one example of each.
questions.answer: यन्त्र are BLUNT instruments used for grasping, holding and extracting — the Samhita describes 101 of them (example: संदंशयन्त्रम्, forceps; the hand, हस्तः, is called the best yantra). शस्त्र are SHARP cutting instruments — 121 are described (example: वृद्धिपत्रम्, a scalpel-like blade).
questions.explanation: Blunt vs sharp, 101 vs 121, with one example each.

questions.question: Describe the structure of the सुश्रुतसंहिता — its two parts, the five sthanas of the first part with their subjects, and the approximate total number of chapters.
questions.answer: The Samhita has two parts. (1) पूर्वतन्त्रम् with five sthanas: सूत्रस्थानम् (fundamental principles, 46 chapters), निदानस्थानम् (diagnosis, 16), शारीरस्थानम् (anatomy and embryology, 10), चिकित्सास्थानम् (treatment, 40), कल्पस्थानम् (toxicology, 8). (2) उत्तरतन्त्रम् (66 chapters) on the eye, ear, nose and other specialised topics. In all there are about 186 chapters.
questions.explanation: Two parts, five sthanas with subjects, ~186 chapters.

questions.question: योग्या (practice/rehearsal) के अनुसार — On which models did Sushruta's students practise (a) incision (छेदनम्), (b) puncturing (वेधनम्), (c) bandaging (बन्धनम्)? Why did they practise on models first?
questions.answer: (a) Incision was practised on gourds and vegetables such as कूष्माण्ड (ash gourd) and अलाबु (bottle gourd); (b) puncturing on the vessels (सिरा) of dead animals and on lotus stalks (पद्मनाल); (c) bandaging on stuffed cloth mannequins (पुत्तलिका). They practised on models first so that the hand would become steady and skilled BEFORE touching a real patient — safe, graded, simulation-based training.
questions.explanation: Skill-to-model mapping plus the safety principle behind योग्या.

questions.question: नासासंधानम् किम्? Explain briefly (as history of science) what this procedure was and why it was needed in those times.
questions.answer: नासासंधानम् is the reconstruction (rebuilding) of a cut nose — rhinoplasty. As the Samhita describes it, a flap of skin was taken from the cheek (गण्ड) and joined to the nose so that a cut nose could be rebuilt. It was needed because in those days the nose was sometimes cut off as a punishment or lost in battle; the operation restored both the face and the person's dignity. It is described here purely as the history of Indian science.
questions.explanation: Definition, cheek-flap method, historical context of nose-cutting, dignity restored.

questions.question: व्याकरणम् — (a) Give the समासविग्रह and the name of the समास of शल्यचिकित्साजनकः. (b) Do the सन्धिविच्छेद of नास्ति. (c) Which प्रत्यय is in ज्ञातुम्?
questions.answer: (a) शल्यचिकित्साजनकः = शल्यचिकित्सायाः जनकः ('father of surgery') — षष्ठीतत्पुरुषसमासः. (b) नास्ति = न + अस्ति (दीर्घसन्धिः, अ + अ = आ). (c) ज्ञातुम् = ज्ञा + तुमुन् प्रत्ययः (infinitive, 'to know').
questions.explanation: Three short grammar tasks drawn directly from the lesson's grammar section.

questions.question: वैद्यधर्मः — Analyse the ethical duties Sushruta lays on the physician (any five), and show how each duty is still expected of doctors and professionals today.
questions.answer: Sushruta's charge to the physician includes: (1) शौचम् — cleanliness of body, dress and instruments; today this is hygiene and sterilisation. (2) दया — compassion; the physician must treat the patient like his own son; today: patient-centred care. (3) सत्यम् — truthfulness in speech; today: honest communication and informed consent. (4) गोपनीयता — never revealing the patient's household matters; today: medical confidentiality. (5) अलुब्धता — freedom from greed; today: ethics against overcharging and exploitation. (6) निरन्तराध्ययनम् — lifelong wide study (एकं शास्त्रम् अधीयानः न विद्यात् शास्त्रनिश्चयम्); today: continuing medical education. Sushruta thus anticipated, over two thousand years ago, almost every clause of a modern code of medical ethics — the duties flow from the same root: the patient's trust must never be betrayed.
questions.explanation: Five or more duties, each mapped to its modern counterpart, with an evaluative conclusion.

questions.question: Translate and explain the verse: समदोषः समाग्निश्च समधातुमलक्रियः । प्रसन्नात्मेन्द्रियमनाः स्वस्थ इत्यभिधीयते ॥ Why is this definition of health called remarkably modern?
questions.answer: Word-by-word: समदोषः = whose doshas are balanced; समाग्निः = whose digestive fire is balanced; समधातुमलक्रियः = whose tissues (धातु) and eliminative functions (मल-क्रिया) are normal; प्रसन्न-आत्म-इन्द्रिय-मनाः = whose spirit, senses and mind are serene; स्वस्थः इति अभिधीयते = is called healthy. Translation: 'He whose doshas, digestive fire, tissues and eliminations are in balance, and whose self, senses and mind are serene — he is called healthy.' It is called remarkably modern because it defines health POSITIVELY — not merely as absence of disease but as balanced body functions PLUS a serene mind and spirit — very close to the modern definition of health as complete physical and mental well-being. The very word स्वस्थ ('established in oneself') carries this idea of inner balance.
questions.explanation: Word meanings, full translation, and the body-plus-mind evaluation of the definition.

questions.question: Describe Sushruta's complete method of training a surgeon — योग्या (practice models for each skill) and the study of anatomy by dissection — and evaluate why medical historians call it the world's first simulation-based medical education.
questions.answer: Sushruta never allowed a beginner to operate on a patient. First came योग्या, graded rehearsal on models matched to each skill: incision (छेदनम्) on soft gourds like कूष्माण्ड and अलाबु; puncturing (वेधनम्) on the vessels of dead animals and lotus stalks; probing (एषणम्) on worm-eaten wood and bamboo; scraping (लेखनम्) on hides; suturing (सीवनम्) on pieces of cloth and soft leather; bandaging (बन्धनम्) on stuffed cloth mannequins (पुत्तलिका); cautery practice on soft flesh pieces. Each model imitates the feel of the real tissue, so the hand learns safely. For anatomy he insisted on direct observation: a properly obtained body, wrapped and kept in still water for seven days, was examined layer by layer by gentle brushing, so the student SAW every structure instead of only reading about it — शास्त्र united with प्रत्यक्ष. Historians call this the first simulation-based medical education because it contains the exact principles of the modern skills-lab: graded difficulty, tissue-like models, repetition before real practice, and dissection-based anatomy — principles that returned to medical colleges only in recent centuries.
questions.explanation: All the skill-model pairs, the dissection method, and an evaluation naming the modern parallels.

questions.question: 'From the Ganga to the world' — evaluate the global legacy of Sushruta: the Arabic translation, the 1794 report in Europe, and his modern title. Why is his work studied today as history of science?
questions.answer: Sushruta's legacy travelled in three great waves. (1) Around the 8th century CE the Sushruta-Samhita was translated into Arabic (known by names such as Kitab-i-Susrud), carrying Indian surgical knowledge to West Asia, from where ideas flowed onward into the wider medieval world. (2) In 1794 the Gentleman's Magazine in Britain published an eyewitness account of an Indian artisan rebuilding a man's nose by the traditional cheek/forehead-flap method descending from नासासंधानम्; European surgeons were astonished, and this report directly stimulated the rebirth of plastic surgery in Europe. (3) In modern times medical historians across the world honour Sushruta as the 'Father of Surgery' — and especially of plastic and reconstructive surgery — and count the Samhita among the earliest systematic surgical textbooks of humanity. His work is studied today as HISTORY of science because it shows how ancient India built systematic, ethical, teachable surgery — instruments, procedures, simulation training, dissection and a code of ethics — while actual medical practice today follows modern evidence-based medicine. Honouring the history and following modern medicine are two different things, and the lesson teaches both distinctions.
questions.explanation: Three waves of legacy plus the history-vs-practice evaluation.

questions.question: सुश्रुतः कस्मिन् नगरे न्यवसत्? (In which city did Sushruta live?)
questions.explanation: Sushruta lived in Varanasi (Kashi), on the bank of the Ganga.

questions.question: सुश्रुतस्य गुरुः कः आसीत्? (Who was Sushruta's teacher?)
questions.explanation: He studied under Divodasa Dhanvantari, the physician-king of Kashi.

questions.question: सुश्रुतः कस्याः विद्यायाः जनकः इति कथ्यते? (Sushruta is called the father of which discipline?)
questions.explanation: He is honoured as शल्यचिकित्साजनकः — the father of surgery.

questions.question: सुश्रुतः कस्याः नद्याः तीरे शिष्यान् अपाठयत्? (On the bank of which river did Sushruta teach his students?)
questions.explanation: He lived and taught on the bank of the Ganga at Varanasi.

questions.question: According to tradition, Sushruta lived approximately in which period?
questions.explanation: Tradition places him centuries before the common era; historians debate the exact date.

questions.question: दिवोदासः कस्य राज्यस्य राजा आसीत्? (Divodasa was the king of which realm?)
questions.explanation: Divodasa Dhanvantari was the physician-king of Kashi (Varanasi).

questions.question: सुश्रुतः मुख्यतया कः आसीत्? (Sushruta was primarily a ...?)
questions.explanation: He was a surgeon (शल्यवैद्यः) and a teacher of surgery.

questions.question: 'शल्यम्' इति शब्दस्य मूलार्थः कः? (What is the root meaning of the word शल्यम्?)
options: a painful foreign body such as an arrow or thorn
questions.answer: a painful foreign body such as an arrow or thorn
questions.explanation: शल्यम् = an object lodged in the body causing pain (arrow, thorn, splinter); its removal named the discipline.

questions.question: सुश्रुतस्य ज्ञानं कस्मिन् ग्रन्थे सङ्गृहीतम्? (In which book is Sushruta's knowledge compiled?)
questions.explanation: His teaching survives as the Sushruta-Samhita.

questions.question: Which statement about our knowledge of Sushruta's life is the most historically careful?
options: Every detail of his life is known from official records
Nothing at all is known about him
His teaching survives in the Samhita and tradition, while his exact dates are debated by historians
He is known only from European books of the 18th century
questions.answer: His teaching survives in the Samhita and tradition, while his exact dates are debated by historians
questions.explanation: Sound history: the text and tradition are firm evidence; precise dating remains debated.

questions.question: सुश्रुतसंहितायाः प्रधानविषयः कः? (What is the main subject of the Sushruta-Samhita?)
questions.explanation: Surgery (Shalya-tantra) is the central discipline of the Samhita.

questions.question: सुश्रुतसंहितायाः द्वौ भागौ कौ? (What are the two parts of the Sushruta-Samhita?)
questions.explanation: The Samhita consists of the Purva-tantra (five sthanas) and the Uttara-tantra.

questions.question: पूर्वतन्त्रे कति स्थानानि सन्ति? (How many sthanas are there in the Purva-tantra?)
questions.explanation: Five: सूत्र, निदान, शारीर, चिकित्सा and कल्प sthanas.

questions.question: शरीररचनायाः (anatomy) वर्णनं कस्मिन् स्थाने अस्ति? (Which sthana deals with the structure of the body?)
questions.explanation: The Sharira-sthana covers anatomy and embryology.

questions.question: सूत्रस्थाने कति अध्यायाः सन्ति? (How many chapters are in the Sutra-sthana?)
questions.explanation: The Sutra-sthana, on fundamental principles, has 46 chapters.

questions.question: चिकित्सास्थानस्य विषयः कः? (What is the subject of the Chikitsa-sthana?)
questions.explanation: चिकित्सा = treatment; this sthana (40 chapters) deals with therapy.

questions.question: कल्पस्थानस्य मुख्यविषयः कः? (What is the main subject of the Kalpa-sthana?)
questions.explanation: The Kalpa-sthana (8 chapters) deals with toxicology.

questions.question: उत्तरतन्त्रे कति अध्यायाः सन्ति? (How many chapters are in the Uttara-tantra?)
questions.explanation: The Uttara-tantra has 66 chapters on specialised subjects.

questions.question: सुश्रुतसंहितायां सर्वे मिलित्वा कति अध्यायाः (approximately)?
questions.explanation: 120 chapters of the Purva-tantra plus 66 of the Uttara-tantra = about 186.

questions.question: सुश्रुतसंहिता कस्यां भाषायां रचिता? (In which language is the Sushruta-Samhita composed?)
questions.explanation: The Samhita is a Sanskrit compendium.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a sthana of the Sushruta-Samhita's Purva-tantra?
questions.explanation: विमानस्थानम् belongs to the Charaka-Samhita, not to Sushruta's Purva-tantra.

questions.question: सुश्रुतसंहितायां कति यन्त्राणि वर्णितानि? (How many yantras are described in the Samhita?)
questions.explanation: 101 blunt instruments (yantras) are described.

questions.question: सुश्रुतसंहितायां कति शस्त्राणि वर्णितानि? (How many shastras are described in the Samhita?)
questions.explanation: 121 sharp instruments (shastras) are described.

questions.question: सुश्रुतमते सर्वेषां यन्त्राणां श्रेष्ठं किम्? (According to Sushruta, which is the best of all yantras?)
questions.explanation: He declared the hand the foremost yantra — no instrument works without it.

questions.question: यन्त्राणि कीदृशानि उपकरणानि? (What kind of instruments are yantras?)
options: blunt instruments for grasping and extracting
questions.answer: blunt instruments for grasping and extracting
questions.explanation: Yantras are blunt tools — for holding, grasping, extracting.

questions.question: शस्त्राणि कीदृशानि? (What kind of instruments are shastras?)
questions.explanation: Shastras are the sharp, cutting instruments (121 in number).

questions.question: बहूनि यन्त्राणि केषाम् आकारेण निर्मितानि? (Many yantras were shaped in the form of what?)
options: the mouths and beaks of animals and birds
questions.answer: the mouths and beaks of animals and birds
questions.explanation: Instruments like सिंहमुखम् ('lion-mouth') were named and shaped after animal mouths and bird beaks.

questions.question: संदंशयन्त्रस्य कार्यं किम्? (What is the function of the sandamsha-yantra?)
questions.explanation: संदंश = forceps/tongs — a grasping (blunt) yantra.

questions.question: सुश्रुतः कति विधानि शस्त्रकर्माणि अवर्णयत्? (How many kinds of surgical operations did Sushruta describe?)
questions.explanation: The अष्टविधशस्त्रकर्माणि — eight kinds of operations.

questions.question: 'सीव्यम्' इति शस्त्रकर्मणः अर्थः कः? (What does the operation called सीव्य mean?)
questions.explanation: सीव्य (from सिव् 'to sew') = suturing.

questions.question: 'आहार्यम्' इति शस्त्रकर्मणः अर्थः कः? (What does आहार्य mean among the eight operations?)
questions.explanation: आहार्य = extraction, e.g. removing a foreign body (शल्य).

questions.question: 'विस्राव्यम्' इति कर्मणः अर्थः कः? (What does विस्राव्य mean?)
questions.explanation: विस्राव्य = letting out / draining fluids from a swelling or wound.

questions.question: 'नासासंधानम्' इत्यस्य अर्थः कः? (What does नासासंधानम् mean?)
questions.explanation: नासा (nose) + संधान (joining) = rhinoplasty, rebuilding a cut nose.

questions.question: नासासंधाने त्वक्खण्डः कुतः गृह्यते स्म? (In rhinoplasty, from where was the skin flap taken?)
questions.explanation: The Samhita describes taking a flap of skin from the cheek to rebuild the nose.

questions.question: Why was nose reconstruction often needed in ancient times?
options: the nose was sometimes cut off as a punishment or lost in battle
it was done for decoration only
questions.answer: the nose was sometimes cut off as a punishment or lost in battle
questions.explanation: Nose-cutting as punishment created the need; the operation restored face and dignity.

questions.question: In the historical couching operation for clouded vision, which instrument was used?
questions.explanation: The clouded lens was displaced with a fine rod called शलाका — described purely as history.

questions.question: What did the ancient couching operation actually do (as history describes it)?
options: displaced the clouded lens out of the line of sight
questions.answer: displaced the clouded lens out of the line of sight
questions.explanation: Couching pushed the clouded lens aside so light could pass — an ancient method, long replaced by modern surgery.

questions.question: 'छेद्यम्' इति कर्मणः अर्थः कः? (What does छेद्य mean?)
questions.explanation: छेद्य = excision, from छिद् 'to cut'.

questions.question: 'भेद्यम्' इति कर्मणः अर्थः कः? (What does भेद्य mean?)
questions.explanation: भेद्य = incision, cutting open (e.g. of a swelling).

questions.question: For suturing internal wounds, the Samhita famously mentions the use of —
questions.explanation: Ant heads gripping the wound edges served as natural clips — a famous historical detail.

questions.question: अस्थिभङ्गे (fracture) का व्यवस्था वर्णिता? (What management of fractures is described?)
questions.explanation: Fractures were supported with splints and firm bandaging.

questions.question: शरीरे कति मर्माणि सुश्रुतः अगणयत्? (How many marmas did Sushruta count in the body?)
questions.explanation: He mapped 107 vital points (marmas).

questions.question: मर्माणि किमर्थं ज्ञातव्यानि? (Why must the marmas be known?)
options: injury at these vital points is dangerous, so the surgeon must protect them
questions.answer: injury at these vital points is dangerous, so the surgeon must protect them
questions.explanation: Marmas are vital points; protecting them was a core rule of safe surgery.

questions.question: How does this lesson present the ancient procedures of the Samhita?
options: as instructions to try at home
as the history of Indian science
questions.answer: as the history of Indian science
questions.explanation: The chapter studies these procedures as history — not as medical guidance.

questions.question: छात्राः छेदनाभ्यासं कुत्र अकुर्वन्? (On what did students practise incision?)
options: on gourds such as कूष्माण्ड and अलाबु
questions.answer: on gourds such as कूष्माण्ड and अलाबु
questions.explanation: Incision was rehearsed on soft gourds and vegetables first.

questions.question: वेधनाभ्यासः कुत्र क्रियते स्म? (On what was puncturing practised?)
options: on lotus stalks and vessels of dead animals
questions.answer: on lotus stalks and vessels of dead animals
questions.explanation: Puncturing was practised on पद्मनाल (lotus stalks) and the सिरा of dead animals.

questions.question: बन्धनाभ्यासः (bandaging practice) कस्याम् उपरि क्रियते स्म?
questions.explanation: Bandaging was rehearsed on full-size stuffed cloth dolls.

questions.question: एषणाभ्यासः (probing practice) कुत्र क्रियते स्म?
questions.explanation: The winding channels of worm-eaten wood (घुणभक्षितं काष्ठम्) imitated sinuses for probing practice.

questions.question: सीवनाभ्यासः (suturing practice) कुत्र क्रियते स्म?
questions.explanation: Suturing was practised on pieces of cloth and soft hide.

questions.question: In Sushruta's dissection method, how was the body prepared for study?
options: it was dried in the sun for a day
it was kept wrapped in still water for seven days and then examined layer by layer
it was studied only from drawings
questions.answer: it was kept wrapped in still water for seven days and then examined layer by layer
questions.explanation: After seven days in still water, gentle brushing revealed the structures layer by layer.

questions.question: सुश्रुतः शवच्छेदनं किमर्थम् आवश्यकं मन्यते स्म? (Why did Sushruta consider dissection necessary?)
options: because knowledge seen directly (प्रत्यक्ष) becomes firm and complete
questions.answer: because knowledge seen directly (प्रत्यक्ष) becomes firm and complete
questions.explanation: He taught that शास्त्र (theory) must be united with direct observation.

questions.question: What single modern principle best matches Sushruta's योग्या system of practising on gourds, stalks and mannequins?
options: simulation-based skills training before real practice
questions.answer: simulation-based skills training before real practice
questions.explanation: Each model imitated real tissue so the hand learned safely — exactly the modern skills-lab principle.

questions.question: 'योग्या' इति शब्दस्य अर्थः अस्मिन् पाठे कः? (What does योग्या mean in this lesson?)
questions.explanation: योग्या = the graded practice a student performs on models before real surgery.

questions.question: वैद्यः रोगिणं कम् इव पश्येत्? (The physician should look upon the patient like whom?)
questions.explanation: Sushruta's charge: treat the patient like your own son.

questions.question: In which chapter of the Samhita is the student's initiation and ethical charge described?
questions.explanation: The Shishyopanayaniya chapter of the Sutra-sthana describes the initiation and the solemn charge.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a quality Sushruta demands of the physician?
questions.explanation: The physician must be अलुब्धः — free from greed; the other three are required.

questions.question: रोगिणः गृहवार्ताविषये वैद्यस्य कर्तव्यं किम्? (What is the physician's duty regarding the patient's household matters?)
options: he should discuss them in the market
he should never reveal them to others
he should write them in a public book
he should tell the king only
questions.answer: he should never reveal them to others
questions.explanation: Strict confidentiality: what is seen or heard in the patient's home must not be told outside.

questions.question: 'एकं शास्त्रमधीयानो न विद्याच्छास्त्रनिश्चयम्' — What does this verse teach the physician?
options: one book is enough for mastery
study of a single science alone cannot give certainty, so one must be widely learned
science has no certainty at all
questions.answer: study of a single science alone cannot give certainty, so one must be widely learned
questions.explanation: The verse commands wide, lifelong study — बहुश्रुतः भवेत् चिकित्सकः.

questions.question: The verse 'समदोषः समाग्निश्च...' from the Sushruta-Samhita gives the definition of —
questions.explanation: It defines health as balanced body functions plus a serene mind, senses and spirit.

questions.question: Sushruta taught that a physician with book-knowledge alone, without practical skill, is incomplete. Which pair expresses this balance?
options: शास्त्रम् and प्रत्यक्षम् (theory and direct practice)
questions.answer: शास्त्रम् and प्रत्यक्षम् (theory and direct practice)
questions.explanation: Theory united with hands-on observation and skill makes knowledge complete.

questions.question: वैद्यः कीदृशः भवेत् इति सुश्रुतः अवदत्? (What kind of person should the physician be, per Sushruta?)
questions.explanation: Clean, compassionate and truthful — the core of वैद्यधर्मः.

questions.question: 'शल्यचिकित्साजनकः' इत्यत्र कः समासः? (Which compound is शल्यचिकित्साजनकः?)
questions.explanation: विग्रहः — शल्यचिकित्सायाः जनकः ('father OF surgery'): genitive Tatpurusha.

questions.question: 'सुश्रुतसंहिता' इत्यस्य समासविग्रहः कः? (What is the compound analysis of सुश्रुतसंहिता?)
questions.explanation: 'The compendium OF Sushruta' — षष्ठीतत्पुरुषः.

questions.question: 'भूत्वा' इत्यत्र कः प्रत्ययः? (Which suffix is in भूत्वा?)
questions.explanation: भू + क्त्वा = भूत्वा, 'having become' — the gerund/absolutive.

questions.question: 'छेत्तुम्' इत्यत्र कः प्रत्ययः? (Which suffix is in छेत्तुम्?)
questions.explanation: छिद् + तुमुन् = छेत्तुम्, 'to cut' — the infinitive.

questions.question: 'गङ्गायाः तीरे' इत्यत्र 'गङ्गायाः' इति पदे का विभक्तिः? (Which case is गङ्गायाः in 'गङ्गायाः तीरे'?)
questions.explanation: गङ्गायाः = 'of the Ganga' — genitive (षष्ठी) singular; तीरे is locative.

questions.question: 'वैद्यः शस्त्रेण व्रणं चिकित्सति' — 'शस्त्रेण' इति पदे का विभक्तिः?
questions.explanation: शस्त्रेण = 'with/by the instrument' — instrumental (तृतीया) singular.

questions.question: 'नास्ति' इत्यस्य सन्धिविच्छेदः कः? (What is the sandhi-split of नास्ति?)
questions.explanation: अ + अ merge into आ (दीर्घसन्धिः): न + अस्ति = नास्ति.

questions.question: 'इत्यभिधीयते' इत्यस्य सन्धिविच्छेदः कः? (What is the sandhi-split of इत्यभिधीयते?)
questions.explanation: इ + अ → य् (यण्-सन्धिः): इति + अभिधीयते = इत्यभिधीयते, from the verse समदोषः...

questions.question: Around the 8th century CE the Sushruta-Samhita was translated into which language?
questions.explanation: It became known in Arabic by names such as Kitab-i-Susrud, spreading its ideas westward.

questions.question: What happened in 1794 CE that spread Sushruta's fame to Europe?
options: the Samhita was printed in Paris
a British magazine published an eyewitness account of an Indian rhinoplasty, astonishing European surgeons
a statue of Sushruta was built in London
questions.answer: a British magazine published an eyewitness account of an Indian rhinoplasty, astonishing European surgeons
questions.explanation: The Gentleman's Magazine report on the Indian nose-rebuilding method stimulated the rebirth of European plastic surgery.

questions.question: By what title is Sushruta honoured in the history of medicine today?
questions.explanation: Medical historians call him the Father of Surgery — especially of plastic surgery.

questions.question: Which modern medical field is the direct descendant of नासासंधानम्?
questions.explanation: Nose reconstruction by skin flap is the ancestor of modern plastic surgery techniques.

questions.question: What is the correct attitude this lesson teaches towards the ancient procedures it describes?
options: honour them as history of science while following modern medicine for actual health care
questions.answer: honour them as history of science while following modern medicine for actual health care
questions.explanation: History is to be studied and honoured; health care belongs to qualified modern doctors.

questions.question: Why do historians count the Sushruta-Samhita among the most important texts in the history of medicine?
options: because it is the longest Sanskrit book
because it is one of the earliest SYSTEMATIC textbooks of surgery — instruments, procedures, training and ethics together
because it was written in Europe
questions.answer: because it is one of the earliest SYSTEMATIC textbooks of surgery — instruments, procedures, training and ethics together
questions.explanation: Its completeness — tools, techniques, pedagogy and ethics — makes it a landmark of human science.

questions.question: सुश्रुतः वाराणसीनगरे गङ्गायाः तीरे न्यवसत्। (Sushruta lived in Varanasi on the bank of the Ganga.)
questions.explanation: True — the lesson places him in Varanasi (Kashi) on the Ganga.

questions.question: The Sushruta-Samhita is mainly a book of astronomy. (सुश्रुतसंहिता मुख्यतया ज्योतिषग्रन्थः अस्ति।)
questions.explanation: False — its central subject is शल्यतन्त्रम् (surgery), within Ayurveda.

questions.question: सुश्रुतसंहितायाम् एकविंशत्यधिकशतं (121) शस्त्राणि वर्णितानि। (The Samhita describes 121 sharp instruments.)
questions.explanation: True — 121 shastras (sharp) and 101 yantras (blunt).

questions.question: According to Sushruta, the hand (हस्तः) is the foremost of all yantras.
questions.explanation: True — no instrument works without the hand, so it is the best yantra.

questions.question: In नासासंधानम्, the Samhita describes rebuilding the nose with a flap of skin taken from the cheek.
questions.explanation: True — the cheek (गण्ड) flap is the described source of skin.

questions.question: सुश्रुतमते शरीरे सप्तोत्तरशतं (107) मर्माणि सन्ति। (According to Sushruta there are 107 marmas in the body.)
questions.explanation: True — 107 vital points, all to be known and protected by the surgeon.

questions.question: Sushruta's students performed their very first practice cuts on real patients.
questions.explanation: False — first came योग्या on gourds, stalks, cloth and mannequins; only trained hands approached patients.

questions.question: Sushruta rejected dissection and taught anatomy only from books. (सुश्रुतः शवच्छेदनं निषिद्धवान्।)
questions.explanation: False — he insisted on supervised dissection so that knowledge would be प्रत्यक्ष (directly seen).

questions.question: According to Sushruta, a physician may freely talk about a patient's household matters with others.
questions.explanation: False — strict confidentiality is part of वैद्यधर्मः: never reveal the patient's private matters.

questions.question: The Sushruta-Samhita was translated into Arabic around the 8th century CE.
questions.explanation: True — known by names such as Kitab-i-Susrud, it carried Indian surgery westward.

questions.question: सुश्रुतः ________ नगरे न्यवसत्। (Sushruta lived in the city of ________ — write the city's name in Devanagari.)
questions.explanation: He lived in वाराणसी (Kashi); in the sentence the locative वाराणस्याम्/वाराणसीनगरे is understood.

questions.question: सुश्रुतस्य गुरुः दिवोदासः ________ आसीत्। (Sushruta's guru was Divodasa ________.)
questions.explanation: His teacher was दिवोदासः धन्वन्तरिः, the physician-king of Kashi.

questions.question: सुश्रुतः ________ जनकः इति कथ्यते। (Sushruta is called the father of ________ — one Sanskrit word in षष्ठी.)
questions.explanation: शल्यचिकित्सायाः जनकः = father of surgery.

questions.question: सुश्रुतसंहिता ________ भाषायां रचिता अस्ति। (The Sushruta-Samhita is composed in the ________ language.)
questions.explanation: It is a Sanskrit (संस्कृत) compendium.

questions.question: संहितायाः द्वौ भागौ — पूर्वतन्त्रम् ________ च। (The two parts of the Samhita are the Purva-tantra and the ________.)
questions.explanation: पूर्वतन्त्रम् (five sthanas) and उत्तरतन्त्रम् (66 chapters).

questions.question: विषचिकित्सायाः वर्णनं ________ स्थाने अस्ति। (The management of poisons is described in the ________ sthana.)
questions.explanation: कल्पस्थानम् (8 chapters) is the toxicology section.

questions.question: सुश्रुतसंहितायां यन्त्राणां संख्या ________ अस्ति। (The number of yantras in the Samhita is ________ — write the number word or figure.)
questions.explanation: 101 blunt instruments (यन्त्राणि) are described.

questions.question: सर्वेषां यन्त्राणां श्रेष्ठः ________ अस्ति। (The best of all yantras is the ________ — one Sanskrit word.)
questions.explanation: The hand (हस्तः) is declared the foremost yantra.

questions.question: शस्त्राणां संख्या ________ अस्ति। (The number of shastras is ________ — write the number word or figure.)
questions.explanation: 121 sharp instruments (शस्त्राणि) are described.

questions.question: छिन्नायाः नासिकायाः पुनर्निर्माणं ________ इति कथ्यते। (The rebuilding of a cut nose is called ________ — one Sanskrit word.)
questions.explanation: नासा + संधानम् = rhinoplasty, Sushruta's most famous procedure.

questions.question: नासासंधाने त्वक्खण्डः ________ गृह्यते स्म। (In rhinoplasty the skin flap was taken from the ________ — one Sanskrit word in पञ्चमी.)
questions.explanation: गण्डात् = from the cheek (पञ्चमी विभक्तिः).

questions.question: छात्राः छेदनाभ्यासं ________ फले अकुर्वन्। (Students practised incision on the ________ gourd — one Sanskrit word.)
questions.explanation: Incision was rehearsed on the ash gourd (कूष्माण्ड) and similar soft fruits.

questions.question: शरीरज्ञानाय सुश्रुतः ________ आवश्यकं मन्यते स्म। (For knowledge of the body Sushruta considered ________ necessary — one Sanskrit word.)
questions.explanation: Dissection (शवच्छेदनम्) gave direct, प्रत्यक्ष anatomical knowledge.

questions.question: वैद्यः रोगिणं ________ इव पश्येत्। (The physician should look upon the patient like a ________ — one Sanskrit word in द्वितीया.)
questions.explanation: पुत्रम् इव = like his own son — Sushruta's ethical charge.

questions.question: 'ज्ञातुम्' इति पदे ________ प्रत्ययः अस्ति। ('ज्ञातुम्' contains the ________ suffix — name the pratyaya.)
questions.explanation: ज्ञा + तुमुन् = ज्ञातुम्, the infinitive 'to know'.

questions.question: सुश्रुतः कः आसीत्? Introduce Sushruta in two or three sentences (Sanskrit or English).
questions.answer: सुश्रुतः प्राचीनभारतस्य महान् शल्यवैद्यः आसीत्। सः वाराणस्यां गङ्गायाः तीरे न्यवसत्, काशिराजस्य दिवोदासस्य धन्वन्तरेः शिष्यः च आसीत्। (Sushruta was a great surgeon of ancient India, who lived in Varanasi on the bank of the Ganga and studied under Divodasa Dhanvantari, king of Kashi. His teaching is preserved in the Sushruta-Samhita.)
questions.explanation: Three identifying facts: profession, place, teacher — plus his book.

questions.question: सुश्रुतः 'शल्यचिकित्साजनकः' इति किमर्थं कथ्यते? (Why is Sushruta called the 'father of surgery'?)
questions.answer: Because he was the first to organise surgery (शल्यतन्त्रम्) into a complete, teachable science — describing instruments, the eight kinds of operations, famous procedures like नासासंधानम्, a training system for students, anatomy by dissection, and the surgeon's ethics — all compiled in the Sushruta-Samhita, one of the earliest systematic surgical textbooks of the world.
questions.explanation: The title rests on systematisation: tools + procedures + training + ethics in one work.

questions.question: सुश्रुतसंहितायाः रचना (structure) संक्षेपेण वर्णयत — its parts, sthanas and total chapters.
questions.answer: The Samhita has two parts: (1) पूर्वतन्त्रम् with five sthanas — सूत्रस्थानम् (principles, 46 chapters), निदानस्थानम् (diagnosis, 16), शारीरस्थानम् (anatomy, 10), चिकित्सास्थानम् (treatment, 40), कल्पस्थानम् (toxicology, 8); and (2) उत्तरतन्त्रम् with 66 chapters on the eye, ear, nose and other special subjects — about 186 chapters in all.
questions.explanation: Two parts, five sthanas with chapter counts, total ~186.

questions.question: 'शल्यम्' इति शब्दस्य कः अर्थः? तेन शल्यतन्त्रम् इति नाम कथं जातम्? (What does शल्यम् mean, and how did it give the discipline its name?)
questions.answer: शल्यम् means a painful foreign body lodged in the flesh — an arrow, thorn or bone splinter. The branch of medicine that removes such objects with instruments and treats wounds was therefore named शल्यतन्त्रम् (the science of the shalya), and its practitioner शल्यवैद्यः — the surgeon.
questions.explanation: Word meaning plus the derivation of the discipline's name.

questions.question: यन्त्र-शस्त्रयोः भेदं सोदाहरणं लिखत। (Write the difference between yantra and shastra with one example each and their numbers.)
questions.answer: यन्त्र are blunt instruments for grasping, holding and extracting — 101 in number; example: संदंशयन्त्रम् (forceps). शस्त्र are sharp cutting instruments — 121 in number; example: वृद्धिपत्रम् (a scalpel-like blade). Sushruta called the hand (हस्तः) the best of all yantras.
questions.explanation: Blunt vs sharp, 101 vs 121, one example each, hand as best.

questions.question: सुश्रुतः हस्तं सर्वयन्त्रश्रेष्ठं किमर्थम् अमन्यत? (Why did Sushruta consider the hand the best of all instruments?)
questions.answer: Because no instrument can act by itself — every yantra and shastra is guided, held and controlled by the hand. The skill, steadiness and judgement of the surgeon's hand decide the success of every operation; therefore the hand is the foremost यन्त्रम्, and training the hand (योग्या) is the heart of surgical education.
questions.explanation: Instruments are extensions of the hand; hence hand-training matters most.

questions.question: अष्टविधशस्त्रकर्माणि लिखत — List the eight kinds of operations described by Sushruta, with the meaning of any four.
questions.answer: The eight are: छेद्यम् (excision — cutting off), भेद्यम् (incision — cutting open), लेख्यम् (scraping), वेध्यम् (puncturing), एष्यम् (probing), आहार्यम् (extraction — taking out), विस्राव्यम् (drainage of fluids), सीव्यम् (suturing — stitching). Any four meanings as above.
questions.explanation: All eight names; meanings of at least four.

questions.question: नासासंधानम् इति किम्? Describe it briefly as history, with the reason it was needed.
questions.answer: नासासंधानम् is the reconstruction of a cut nose (rhinoplasty). As the Samhita describes, a measured flap of skin was taken from the cheek (गण्ड) and joined over the nose so that the nose was rebuilt. It was needed because the nose was sometimes cut off as punishment or lost in battle; the operation restored both the face and the person's dignity. It is studied today as a landmark in the history of plastic surgery — not as a medical instruction.
questions.explanation: Definition, cheek-flap, historical need, history-not-advice framing.

questions.question: Describe, as history of science, the ancient couching operation for clouded vision mentioned in the lesson.
questions.answer: In the ancient couching operation, the physician used a fine probe called शलाका to displace the clouded lens of the eye downward, out of the line of sight, so that light could again reach the interior and some vision returned. This was one of the earliest recorded operations on the eye. It is described here purely as history: modern cataract surgery is entirely different and far safer, and eye disease today needs a qualified modern doctor.
questions.explanation: Shalaka, displacement of the clouded lens, historical framing with the modern caveat.

questions.question: मर्म किम्? मर्मज्ञानं शल्यवैद्यस्य किमर्थम् आवश्यकम्? (What is a marma? Why must a surgeon know the marmas?)
questions.answer: A मर्म is a vital point of the body — a spot where muscles, vessels, sinews, bones and joints meet and where injury is especially dangerous. Sushruta counted 107 marmas. A surgeon must know them all so that his incisions and instruments AVOID these points — protecting the patient's life during every operation.
questions.explanation: Definition, the number 107, and the protective purpose.

questions.question: सीवनार्थं (for suturing) के के साधनानि संहितायां वर्णितानि? (What suturing materials does the Samhita describe?)
questions.answer: Threads of plant fibre (such as flax/hemp), hair, and — most famously — the heads of large black ants for internal wounds: the ant's jaws gripped the wound edges together and the body was removed, leaving the head as a natural clip. Needles (सूची) of different shapes were used for different parts.
questions.explanation: Threads, hair, ant-heads as natural clips, shaped needles.

questions.question: योग्या-पद्धत्या कः अभ्यासः कुत्र क्रियते स्म? Match any four skills to their practice models.
questions.answer: (1) छेदनम् (incision) — on gourds like कूष्माण्ड and अलाबु; (2) वेधनम् (puncturing) — on lotus stalks and the vessels of dead animals; (3) एषणम् (probing) — on worm-eaten wood and bamboo; (4) सीवनम् (suturing) — on cloth and soft leather; (5) बन्धनम् (bandaging) — on stuffed cloth mannequins (पुत्तलिका); (6) लेखनम् (scraping) — on hides. (Any four pairs.)
questions.explanation: Skill-model pairs from the योग्या system.

questions.question: सुश्रुतस्य शवच्छेदनविधिं वर्णयत। (Describe Sushruta's method of dissection for the study of anatomy.)
questions.answer: A properly obtained dead body was cleaned, wrapped (in grass/bark coverings), and kept submerged in still water for seven days. Then the teacher and students brushed the softened surface away layer by layer, observing skin, muscles, vessels and inner organs one by one. In this way the student SAW every structure directly (प्रत्यक्ष) instead of only reading about it — making anatomical knowledge firm and complete.
questions.explanation: Seven-day water preparation, layer-by-layer brushing, direct observation.

questions.question: आदौ आदर्शेषु (models) अभ्यासः, पश्चात् रोगिषु — अस्याः पद्धतेः त्रीणि कारणानि लिखत। (Give three reasons why practising on models BEFORE patients is wise.)
questions.answer: (1) Safety — a beginner's mistakes fall on a gourd or cloth, not on a living person. (2) Skill-building — repetition on tissue-like materials trains the hand until cutting, probing and stitching become steady and precise. (3) Confidence and grading — the student advances step by step from easy models to harder ones, and the teacher can test competence before allowing real practice. This is exactly the principle of the modern simulation lab.
questions.explanation: Safety, motor-skill repetition, graded assessment — with the modern parallel.

questions.question: सुश्रुतमते वैद्यस्य के गुणाः भवेयुः? (What qualities should a physician have according to Sushruta? Give at least four with brief meanings.)
questions.answer: The physician should be: शुचिः — clean in body, dress and instruments; दयालुः — compassionate towards every patient; सत्यवादी — truthful in speech; अलुब्धः — free from greed; and he should treat the patient पुत्रम् इव — like his own son, keep the patient's household matters secret, and continue studying widely throughout life.
questions.explanation: Four-plus qualities: cleanliness, compassion, truthfulness, non-greed, plus son-like care and confidentiality.

questions.question: 'रोगिणः गृहवार्तां बहिः न कथयेत्' — Explain this duty and show why it is still central to medical ethics today.
questions.answer: The rule commands confidentiality: whatever the physician sees or hears in the patient's home — illness, family matters, private circumstances — must never be told outside. It protects the patient's dignity and, more deeply, the TRUST on which all healing depends: a patient will speak openly only to a doctor who keeps secrets. Modern medical ethics contains the same clause (patient confidentiality), and modern laws protect medical privacy — showing that Sushruta identified a permanent foundation of the doctor-patient relationship.
questions.explanation: Meaning of the rule, the trust argument, and the modern parallel.

questions.question: समासविग्रहं समासनाम च लिखत — (a) शल्यचिकित्साजनकः (b) नासासंधानम्.
questions.answer: (a) शल्यचिकित्साजनकः = शल्यचिकित्सायाः जनकः ('father of surgery') — षष्ठीतत्पुरुषसमासः. (b) नासासंधानम् = नासायाः संधानम् ('joining of the nose') — षष्ठीतत्पुरुषसमासः.
questions.explanation: Both are genitive Tatpurusha compounds; the first member stands in षष्ठी in the विग्रह.

questions.question: कृदन्तपदानि पृथक् कुरुत — Identify the root and suffix: (a) भूत्वा (b) छेत्तुम् (c) सङ्गृहीतम्.
questions.answer: (a) भूत्वा = भू + क्त्वा ('having become' — absolutive). (b) छेत्तुम् = छिद् + तुमुन् ('to cut' — infinitive). (c) सङ्गृहीतम् = सम् + ग्रह् + क्त ('compiled' — past passive participle).
questions.explanation: क्त्वा, तुमुन् and क्त — the three kridanta suffixes taught in the lesson.

questions.question: अधोलिखिते वाक्ये रेखाङ्कितपदानां विभक्तिं लिखत — 'गुरुः शिष्येभ्यः शल्यतन्त्रं गण्डात् गृहीतेन त्वक्खण्डेन अपाठयत्' : (a) शिष्येभ्यः (b) गण्डात् (c) त्वक्खण्डेन.
questions.answer: (a) शिष्येभ्यः — चतुर्थी विभक्तिः, बहुवचनम् ('to the students'). (b) गण्डात् — पञ्चमी विभक्तिः, एकवचनम् ('from the cheek'). (c) त्वक्खण्डेन — तृतीया विभक्तिः, एकवचनम् ('with the piece of skin').
questions.explanation: Dative of the receiver, ablative of the source, instrumental of the means.

questions.question: Translate into English and explain in one sentence: समदोषः समाग्निश्च समधातुमलक्रियः । प्रसन्नात्मेन्द्रियमनाः स्वस्थ इत्यभिधीयते ॥
questions.answer: Translation: 'He whose doshas, digestive fire, tissues and eliminative functions are balanced, and whose spirit, senses and mind are serene — he is called healthy (स्वस्थ).' Explanation: health here is defined positively as balance of body PLUS serenity of mind — strikingly close to the modern definition of health as complete physical and mental well-being, not merely absence of disease.
questions.explanation: Full translation plus the body-and-mind evaluation.

questions.question: How did the Sushruta-Samhita reach the Arabic-speaking world, and by what name was it known there?
questions.answer: Around the 8th century CE, during the great translation movement, the Samhita was rendered into Arabic and became known by names such as 'Kitab-i-Susrud' (the Book of Sushruta). Through this translation, Indian surgical knowledge travelled to West Asia and influenced physicians of the medieval Islamic world, from where ideas moved further toward Europe.
questions.explanation: 8th-century Arabic translation, Kitab-i-Susrud, westward transmission.

questions.question: What happened in 1794 CE, and why is that event a turning point in the history of plastic surgery?
questions.answer: In 1794 the Gentleman's Magazine of London published an eyewitness account, with an illustration, of an Indian artisan rebuilding the nose of a man (whose nose had been cut off) by the traditional Indian flap method descended from Sushruta's नासासंधानम्. European surgeons, who had no comparable technique, were astonished; the report was studied and the method was soon attempted in Europe. Historians therefore treat 1794 as the spark of modern European plastic surgery — a direct bridge from Sushruta's ancient craft to the modern operating theatre.
questions.explanation: The 1794 report, Europe's astonishment, and the bridge-to-modernity evaluation.

questions.question: 'वाराणस्याः महान् आचार्यः' — Write an essay on the life of Sushruta: his city, his teacher, his period, his work as a teacher of surgery, and the reason history honours him as शल्यचिकित्साजनकः.
questions.answer: Sushruta was a great physician-teacher of ancient India who lived in वाराणसी (Kashi) on the bank of the Ganga. Tradition makes him the disciple of दिवोदासः धन्वन्तरिः, the physician-king of Kashi, from whom he learnt Ayurveda and above all शल्यतन्त्रम् — surgery. Tradition places him many centuries before the common era (often around the 7th–6th century BCE); historians debate the exact date, but his teaching survives securely in the सुश्रुतसंहिता. As an acharya he trained generations of students, insisting that they rehearse every skill on models (योग्या) before touching a patient, learn anatomy by direct observation, and bind themselves to a strict ethical charge. History honours him as शल्यचिकित्साजनकः because he did what no one before him is known to have done: he organised surgery into a COMPLETE teachable science — 101 yantras and 121 shastras, eight kinds of operations, procedures such as नासासंधानम्, systematic training, anatomy and ethics — all in one compendium that later travelled across the world.
questions.explanation: City, guru, period with the historian's caution, pedagogy, and the systematisation argument for his title.

questions.question: Describe in detail the structure and contents of the सुश्रुतसंहिता — its two parts, each sthana with its subject and chapter count, and what makes शल्यतन्त्र central to the whole work.
questions.answer: The Sushruta-Samhita is arranged in two parts. The पूर्वतन्त्रम् contains five sthanas: (1) सूत्रस्थानम् — 46 chapters on fundamental principles: the surgeon's training, instruments, the eight operations, bandages, diet and the seasons; (2) निदानस्थानम् — 16 chapters on the diagnosis of diseases; (3) शारीरस्थानम् — 10 chapters on anatomy and embryology, including the method of dissection; (4) चिकित्सास्थानम् — 40 chapters on treatment; (5) कल्पस्थानम् — 8 chapters on poisons and their management (toxicology). The उत्तरतन्त्रम् adds 66 chapters on specialised subjects — diseases of the eye (including the historical couching operation), ear, nose and more — bringing the whole to about 186 chapters. शल्यतन्त्र is central because Sushruta held it the foremost branch of medicine: it acts quickly and visibly, its results can be seen at once, and it demands the union of knowledge and handcraft. Every part of the book serves the making of a complete surgeon — principles, diagnosis, anatomy, treatment, poisons and the special organs.
questions.explanation: All five sthanas with counts, the Uttara-tantra, ~186 total, and the argument for surgery's centrality.

questions.question: 'यन्त्राणि शस्त्राणि च' — Write in detail about the surgical instruments of the Sushruta-Samhita: their two classes and numbers, the naming system, the place of the hand, and the eight kinds of operations they served.
questions.answer: The Samhita describes 222 instruments in two classes. The 101 यन्त्र are blunt instruments — for grasping, holding, pressing and extracting — such as the संदंश (forceps) and tubular instruments (नाडीयन्त्र); the 121 शस्त्र are sharp instruments for cutting and piercing, such as the वृद्धिपत्र (a scalpel-like blade). Many instruments were shaped and named after the mouths and beaks of animals and birds — सिंहमुखम् ('lion-mouth') and various 'heron-beak' style forceps — a brilliant system that told the craftsman the shape and the student the grip at a single glance. Above them all Sushruta placed the हस्तः, the hand: no instrument moves without it, so the trained hand is the true foremost yantra. These instruments served the अष्टविधशस्त्रकर्माणि, the eight operations: छेद्य (excision), भेद्य (incision), लेख्य (scraping), वेध्य (puncturing), एष्य (probing), आहार्य (extraction), विस्राव्य (drainage) and सीव्य (suturing). Together the classification, naming and hand-first principle show an astonishingly modern engineering mind at work over two thousand years ago.
questions.explanation: Both classes with numbers and examples, animal-naming, hand-first principle, all eight operations.

questions.question: 'नासासंधानम् — the crown of ancient surgery.' Describe the procedure as the Samhita presents it (as history), analyse why it was needed in that society, and explain why the world regards it as the beginning of plastic surgery.
questions.answer: THE PROCEDURE (as history): the Samhita directs the surgeon to measure the lost nose with a leaf, then take a flap of living skin of that size from the cheek (गण्ड), keeping it attached at one end so its blood supply survives; the flap is turned and set over the freshened nasal stump, stitched in place, supported with two small tubes in the nostrils so the patient can breathe, and dressed with healing powders and bandages until it unites. THE NEED: in that age the nose was sometimes cut off as a judicial punishment or lost in battle; a person without a nose lost face in every sense — so the operation restored breath, appearance and dignity, and society valued it highly. THE LEGACY: this is the earliest systematic description of reconstructing a body part with a living skin flap — the exact founding principle of plastic surgery. The Indian method, kept alive by artisan families, was witnessed and reported in 1794, astonished Europe, and seeded modern rhinoplasty. Hence historians of medicine everywhere call नासासंधानम् the beginning of plastic and reconstructive surgery — while today's students study it strictly as history, since real treatment belongs to modern medicine.
questions.explanation: Procedure, social analysis, and the flap-principle argument for its world-historical status.

questions.question: 'सुश्रुतः — the first teacher of simulation.' Describe his complete training system (योग्या models for each skill and dissection for anatomy) and evaluate it against the way modern medical colleges train surgeons.
questions.answer: SUSHRUTA'S SYSTEM: the student was initiated with an ethical charge, then trained by योग्या — graded rehearsal on models chosen to imitate real tissue: incision on soft gourds (कूष्माण्ड, अलाबु, cucumber), puncturing on lotus stalks and the vessels of dead animals, probing on worm-eaten wood and bamboo, scraping on hides, suturing on cloth and soft leather, bandaging on stuffed mannequins (पुत्तलिका), and cautery practice on soft flesh pieces. Anatomy came from supervised dissection: a body prepared in still water for seven days was examined layer by layer, so knowledge was प्रत्यक्ष — directly seen — and not merely read. Only the student whose hand and knowledge were proven approached patients. MODERN COMPARISON: today's colleges use exactly the same architecture — skills labs with synthetic tissue and simulators (the modern gourds and mannequins), cadaver dissection for anatomy, graded competence tests before clinical work, and an ethical oath at entry. EVALUATION: Sushruta's system anticipated every principle — safety of the patient, repetition for motor skill, model-to-reality grading, seeing before doing — which is why medical educators call it the world's first simulation-based surgical curriculum; the tools have changed, the pedagogy has not.
questions.explanation: Full yogya inventory, dissection, and a point-by-point modern comparison.

questions.question: 'वैद्यधर्मः तदा अधुना च' — Present Sushruta's code of ethics for the physician (with reference to the शिष्योपनयनीय charge and the verse एकं शास्त्रम्...), and evaluate how far it matches the ethics expected of a modern doctor.
questions.answer: SUSHRUTA'S CODE: at initiation (शिष्योपनयनीयम्) the teacher binds the student: be शुचिः (clean in person, dress and instruments), दयालुः (compassionate), सत्यवादी (truthful), अलुब्धः (free of greed); treat the patient पुत्रम् इव — like your own son; never reveal the patient's household matters (confidentiality); serve the suffering even at cost to yourself; and never stop learning — for एकं शास्त्रमधीयानो न विद्याच्छास्त्रनिश्चयम्: one science alone gives no certainty, so the physician must be बहुश्रुतः, widely learned. MODERN MATCH: every clause has a modern twin — sterile technique and hygiene; patient-centred, compassionate care; informed, honest communication; medical confidentiality protected by codes and law; ethical limits on fees; and mandatory continuing medical education. EVALUATION: the match is almost complete because both codes grow from the same root — the patient's absolute trust in the healer. Where they differ is mainly in machinery (modern regulation, licensing, documentation), not in spirit. That a teacher on the banks of the Ganga articulated this ethic millennia ago is among the proudest chapters of India's intellectual history.
questions.explanation: The initiation charge, the wide-study verse, clause-by-clause modern mapping, and the trust-based evaluation.

questions.question: व्याकरणकार्यम् — (a) Write THREE simple Sanskrit sentences of your own about Sushruta, using: one षष्ठी form, one तृतीया form, and one क्त्वा (gerund) form. (b) Give the समासविग्रह of सुश्रुतसंहिता and the सन्धिविच्छेद of नास्ति.
questions.answer: (a) Model sentences: (1) सुश्रुतस्य ग्रन्थः जगति प्रसिद्धः अस्ति। (षष्ठी: सुश्रुतस्य — 'Sushruta's book is famous in the world.') (2) वैद्यः शस्त्रेण शल्यं निष्कासयति। (तृतीया: शस्त्रेण — 'The physician removes the foreign body with an instrument.') (3) छात्राः कूष्माण्डे अभ्यासं कृत्वा शल्यकर्म अशिक्षन्त। (क्त्वा: कृत्वा — 'Having practised on a gourd, the students learnt surgery.') Any grammatically correct sentences with the required forms deserve marks. (b) सुश्रुतसंहिता = सुश्रुतस्य संहिता — षष्ठीतत्पुरुषसमासः; नास्ति = न + अस्ति (दीर्घसन्धिः, अ + अ = आ).
questions.explanation: Original composition testing the three required forms, plus the set samasa and sandhi tasks.

questions.question: 'From Varanasi to the world' — Trace and evaluate the global journey of Sushruta's legacy: the Arabic translation, the 1794 European encounter, his modern titles, and the right way for a student of today to relate to this heritage.
questions.answer: THE JOURNEY: (1) Composed in Sanskrit in ancient Varanasi, the Samhita was translated into Arabic around the 8th century CE (known by names such as Kitab-i-Susrud) during the great translation movement, and its ideas entered the medicine of West Asia. (2) In India the craft of नासासंधानम् survived among practitioner families; in 1794 the Gentleman's Magazine published an eyewitness account of such a nose reconstruction, and European surgeons — possessing nothing comparable — studied and revived the method, igniting modern plastic surgery. (3) Today the world's medical historians honour Sushruta as the Father of Surgery, and especially of plastic and reconstructive surgery, and count his Samhita among the earliest systematic surgical textbooks of mankind. EVALUATION: the legacy shows that scientific knowledge travels across languages and centuries when it is systematic, written and teachable — exactly the qualities Sushruta gave his subject. THE RIGHT RELATION: a student should feel informed pride — honouring this heritage as history of Indian science, studying its Sanskrit sources, and at the same time clearly understanding that actual health care today belongs to modern, evidence-based medicine practised by qualified doctors. Pride in history and trust in modern medicine stand together, not against each other.
questions.explanation: Three-stage journey, the transmissibility evaluation, and the history-vs-practice conclusion.

questions.question: PASSAGE: A museum in Varanasi opens a gallery called 'सुश्रुतः — काश्याः महावैद्यः'. The first panel shows a teacher seated by the Ganga with students; the caption says he learnt his science from the physician-king of Kashi and that his teaching became a famous Sanskrit compendium. QUESTIONS: (a) Name the teacher of the gallery's hero. (b) What is the compendium called? (c) Why does the gallery title call him काश्याः महावैद्यः?
questions.answer: (a) His teacher was दिवोदासः धन्वन्तरिः, the physician-king of Kashi. (b) The compendium is the सुश्रुतसंहिता. (c) Because Sushruta lived, learnt and taught in Kashi (Varanasi) on the bank of the Ganga, and became its greatest physician — the father of surgery.
questions.explanation: Reading comprehension anchored on the three life facts.

questions.question: PASSAGE: A librarian is cataloguing an old manuscript of the Sushruta-Samhita. She finds five sections in the first part, and a further long section of 66 chapters at the end dealing with diseases of the eye and ear. QUESTIONS: (a) What are the names of the five sections of the first part? (b) What is the 66-chapter section called? (c) In which of the five sections would she find the rules for the surgeon's basic training and instruments?
questions.answer: (a) The five sthanas of the पूर्वतन्त्रम्: सूत्रस्थानम्, निदानस्थानम्, शारीरस्थानम्, चिकित्सास्थानम्, कल्पस्थानम्. (b) The 66-chapter section is the उत्तरतन्त्रम्. (c) In the सूत्रस्थानम् — the section of fundamental principles, which covers the surgeon's training, instruments and the eight operations.
questions.explanation: Applies the structure of the Samhita to a cataloguing situation.

questions.question: PASSAGE (Sanskrit): आचार्यः सुश्रुतः शिष्यान् उवाच — 'यन्त्राणि बहूनि सन्ति, परं सर्वेषां यन्त्राणां हस्तः एव श्रेष्ठः। हस्तं विना किमपि यन्त्रं न प्रवर्तते। अतः प्रथमं हस्तः एव शिक्षणीयः।' QUESTIONS: (a) What does Sushruta call the best of all yantras, and why? (b) What must therefore be trained first? (c) Translate the middle sentence (हस्तं विना ... न प्रवर्तते) into English.
questions.answer: (a) The hand (हस्तः) — because without it no instrument can function. (b) Therefore the hand itself must be trained first (through योग्या practice). (c) Translation: 'Without the hand, no instrument at all works/operates.'
questions.explanation: Sanskrit comprehension of the hand-first principle.

questions.question: PASSAGE: In a history-of-science exhibition, a showcase displays ancient surgical instruments: one is a grasping tool shaped like a lion's mouth; another is a thin sharp blade. The label says the ancient text lists 101 of one class and 121 of the other. QUESTIONS: (a) To which class does each displayed instrument belong? (b) Which class has 101 and which 121? (c) What advantage did the animal-mouth naming system give?
questions.answer: (a) The lion-mouth grasping tool (सिंहमुखम्) is a यन्त्रम् (blunt instrument); the thin sharp blade is a शस्त्रम् (sharp instrument). (b) Yantras number 101; shastras number 121. (c) Naming instruments after animal mouths and beaks told the craftsman the exact shape to make and told the student the grip and use at a glance — an easy-to-remember design language.
questions.explanation: Classification plus analysis of the naming system's purpose.

questions.question: PASSAGE (history): A traveller in ancient Kashi records: 'I saw a man whose nose had been cut off as a punishment. The surgeon measured the wound with a leaf, took skin from the man's cheek keeping one end attached, turned it over the nose, stitched it, and placed two small tubes in the nostrils.' QUESTIONS: (a) Name this procedure in Sanskrit. (b) Why was one end of the flap kept attached? (c) What was the purpose of the two tubes? (Answer as history of science.)
questions.answer: (a) The procedure is नासासंधानम् (rhinoplasty). (b) One end of the flap stayed attached so the living skin kept its blood supply and could survive and unite in its new place. (c) The two tubes kept the new nostrils open so the patient could breathe while the flap healed and the nose kept its shape. All of this is described as the history of ancient Indian surgery.
questions.explanation: Comprehension of the classic flap procedure with its two technical details.

questions.question: PASSAGE (history): An old text describes an elderly scribe who 'saw the world as through mist; the pupil of his eye had turned cloudy-white.' The ancient physician, the text says, 'took a fine rod and displaced the cloud downward, and light returned.' QUESTIONS: (a) Which eye condition (in the lesson's historical terms) is being described? (b) What was the fine rod called and what did the ancient operation do? (c) Why must a student today read this ONLY as history?
questions.answer: (a) The clouding of the lens — the condition treated in the ancient couching operation (the lesson's तिमिर/clouded-lens condition). (b) The rod was the शलाका; the couching operation pushed the clouded lens out of the line of sight so light could reach the eye again. (c) Because it is ancient history: modern cataract surgery is completely different and far safer, and any real eye problem needs a qualified modern doctor — the lesson teaches the history of science, not medical practice.
questions.explanation: Historical identification, the shalaka mechanism, and the history-not-advice reasoning.

questions.question: PASSAGE: A new student joins Sushruta's school and is eager to treat patients at once. The acharya smiles and hands him an ash gourd and a small blade: 'First a hundred cuts here. Then lotus stalks. Then cloth and needle. The patient comes last.' QUESTIONS: (a) What is this training method called in the lesson? (b) Which skills do the gourd, the lotus stalk and the cloth each train? (c) What principle is the acharya teaching by putting the patient last?
questions.answer: (a) The method is योग्या — graded practical rehearsal on models. (b) The gourd trains incision (छेदनम्); the lotus stalk trains puncturing (वेधनम्); the cloth trains suturing (सीवनम्). (c) The principle: skill must be perfected safely on models BEFORE a living patient is touched — the patient's safety comes first, which is exactly the modern principle of simulation-based training.
questions.explanation: Applies the yogya skill-model pairs and extracts the safety principle.

questions.question: PASSAGE: In the शारीरस्थान class, the acharya leads students to a riverside enclosure. A properly obtained body, wrapped in grass coverings, has lain in still water for seven days. 'Now,' he says, 'brush gently, layer by layer, and SEE — for what is seen is never forgotten.' QUESTIONS: (a) What is this method called and what is its purpose? (b) Why the seven days in water? (c) Which principle of Sushruta's epistemology does 'what is seen is never forgotten' express?
questions.answer: (a) This is शवच्छेदनम् — dissection of the dead body — whose purpose is direct study of human anatomy. (b) The days in still water softened the body so its layers could be separated by gentle brushing, revealing structures one by one without cutting them apart. (c) It expresses the principle of प्रत्यक्ष — direct observation: theory (शास्त्र) must be united with what the student sees with his own eyes for knowledge to be firm and complete.
questions.explanation: Dissection method, the preparation's purpose, and the pratyaksha principle.

questions.question: PASSAGE: At the initiation ceremony, the acharya charges the new student: 'त्वं शुचिः भव। रोगिणं पुत्रम् इव पश्य। रोगिणः गृहे यत् पश्यसि यत् शृणोषि, तत् बहिः मा कथय। लोभं त्यज।' Later, in the town, a merchant offers the student money to reveal what illness a rival suffers from. QUESTIONS: (a) Translate any two commands of the charge. (b) What must the student answer to the merchant, and which duty binds him? (c) Name the modern professional value that matches this duty.
questions.answer: (a) Examples: 'Be clean/pure' (त्वं शुचिः भव); 'Look upon the patient like your own son' (रोगिणं पुत्रम् इव पश्य); 'What you see or hear in the patient's house, do not tell outside'; 'Abandon greed'. (Any two.) (b) He must refuse the money and reveal nothing — bound by the duty of confidentiality (and freedom from greed) in his teacher's charge. (c) The modern value is medical/professional confidentiality — protecting patient privacy against any inducement.
questions.explanation: Translation, application of the ethical charge to a temptation, and the modern parallel.

questions.question: PASSAGE: In 8th-century Baghdad, a scholar completes an Arabic rendering of an Indian book on surgery, calling it the 'Book of Susrud'. A thousand years later, in 1794, a London magazine prints an eyewitness account of an Indian nose reconstruction, and European surgeons begin to study 'the Indian method'. QUESTIONS: (a) Which Sanskrit work is the 'Book of Susrud'? (b) What does this two-stage story show about how knowledge travels? (c) What title has the world consequently given to the author of that Sanskrit work?
questions.answer: (a) The सुश्रुतसंहिता — the Sushruta-Samhita (Arabic: Kitab-i-Susrud). (b) It shows that written, systematic knowledge travels across languages and centuries: first through the Arabic translation movement to West Asia, then through a printed European report that revived the Indian flap method — sparking modern plastic surgery. Systematic recording made the knowledge transmissible. (c) The world honours Sushruta as the 'Father of Surgery' — especially of plastic (reconstructive) surgery.
questions.explanation: Legacy synthesis: translation, transmission and the modern title.
